cohort: The cohort consisted of 19,560 women aged 35 years or older with single pregnancies who delivered at a tertiary hospital in China between 2014 and 2020.
finding: Very advanced maternal age (vAMA) women have an increased risk of gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, cesarean delivery, placenta previa, and adherent placenta compared to advanced maternal age (AMA) women, with gestational hypertension, placenta previa, and adherent placenta identified as key risks for preterm birth and low birth weight.
mod_finding: The AMA group exhibited an increased rate of spontaneous deliveries and precipitated labor, while the vAMA group had a higher rate of cesarean delivery.
gest_age: 28-34 weeks for very preterm births, also included moderate preterm birth
